expectations.text: Distinguishes replication copying deletion from a backup retaining earlier restorable state under retention policy.
expectations.evidence: "It copies changes to another instance, including accidental deletions" and "A backup preserves an earlier state that can be restored, subject to the backup's retention policy" preserve the actual distinction.

expectations.text: Preserves availability versus point-in-time recovery distinction.
expectations.evidence: "Replication can improve availability, but it does not by itself provide point-in-time recovery" states the limitation precisely.

expectations.text: Requires both base backup and unbroken write-ahead logs for this system.
expectations.evidence: "For this system, point-in-time recovery additionally requires a base backup and an unbroken sequence of write-ahead logs" includes both requirements.

expectations.text: No zero-downtime or zero-data-loss promise; 100–150 words.
expectations.evidence: 107 whitespace-delimited words; the modest "can improve availability" and "verify that the required backup and log sequence are retained" make no zero-downtime or zero-loss promise.
